text:
ryan: Heads up — after the kube-proxy 1.27 deployment in eu-west1 we're seeing a sharp drop in traced spans for gpu-serving pods. traceparent header vanishes on ~10-15% of requests when the node flip happens. anyone else seeing this?

maya: when did the upgrade roll out?

kube-upgrade-bot: kube-proxy v1.27 rolled to eu-west1 on 2026-03-16 02:12 UTC, batch size 3 nodes per AZ. :rocket:

ryan: it started right after that rollout. quick example from client logs — request goes out with traceparent, but downstream nginx/access.log shows no trace headers: 

```
client->ingress: traceparent=00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
ingress->gpu-pod: no traceparent header present
```

anita: could be session affinity / conntracking churn. kube-proxy mode changed default conntrack timeout? iptables -> ipvs behaviors differ on connection handoff.

zhao: also check sidecar (envoy) xff/preserve_remote_addr settings — sometimes the header proxying gets overwritten on reconnects.

ryan: our services are behind nginx-ingress (controller v1.8) with proxy_buffering on. config has `proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent;` but seems intermittent.

maya: can you paste otel-collector logs around a missing-span request id?

ryan: pasted a minimal trace from collector: 

```
2026-03-16T02:15:21Z WARN traceprocessor: incoming request without traceparent, creating new trace id, span_count=1 service=gpu-serving
2026-03-16T02:15:21Z INFO exporter: dropped span: reason=orphaned, upstream_id=none
```

anita: hm. conntrack rebalancing can open a new TCP session to backend which loses in-flight headers if the ingress rewrites them on the new handshake. ipvs vs iptables matter. what kube-proxy mode are we on for eu-west1?

ryan: cluster is using iptables mode. kube-proxy configmap shows `conntrack-max-per-core: 0` and default timeouts.

zhao: two quick mitigation ideas:
- enable service.sessionAffinity: ClientIP for the gpu-serving Service (cheap, fast)
- set kube-proxy to keepalives/preserve ports or switch to ipvs with persistent-conn track

maya: both will change L4 routing and have tradeoffs for autoscaler. we should test sessionAffinity in canary namespace first.

ryan: filed a quick PoC: applied `sessionAffinity: ClientIP` on a canary svc. traces for that service recovered to baseline immediately. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident-note created: #IO-4382 "traceparent loss after kube-proxy upgrade (eu-west1)" assigned to @ryan, severity: S2

anita: long-term, we should make tracing resilient to header loss: add fallback instrumentation that injects an external trace id from a cookie or request param if traceparent absent, and alert on trace/request ratio.

zhao: agreed. also update nginx config to always forward trace headers and make sure envoy sidecars don't sanitize them. snippet: 

```nginx
proxy_set_header Traceparent $http_traceparent;
proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
proxy_hide_header Traceparent; # don't hide downstream
```

ryan: for observability: set a Prometheus alert to detect span rate drop vs request rate. here's a quick query we used in the PoC: 

```
(sum(rate(otel_spans_added_total[5m])) by (service)) / (sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) by (service)) < 0.6
```

and alert if ratio < 0.7 for 10m. put this on the gpu-serving service dashboard.

maya: nice. also add a grafana panel comparing `trace_latency` and `request_latency` to spot changed tails.

anita: ops plan: 1) keep sessionAffinity on canary for 24h 2) add Prometheus alert + dashboard panel 3) test ipvs mode on staging 4) consider kube-proxy rollback if broader impact.

ryan: will run canary now and post results. thanks all. :pray:

zhao: FYI I've opened a k8s issue link with similar symptoms, might be a kube-proxy bug with conntrack handoff and header flushing: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/XXXXX

ryan: update — after enabling sessionAffinity on canary for 2 hours traces stayed consistent. I'm scheduling a limited roll for the rest of eu-west1 tonight at 01:00 UTC to flip sessionAffinity for gpu-serving services. will monitor the new alert.

maya: great. if anything spikes ping #oncall and @anita.

ops-bot: monitoring-runbook attached: /runbooks/trace-loss-kubeproxy.md

ryan: closing loop here when roll finishes, thanks everyone! :v:
